candidates.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: supplemental square feature close-up for a custodial-training image library
Input images: Image 1 is the sole anatomy-only reference. Use it only to understand the assembled mechanical relationship of a traditional straight pipe wrench. Generate a new original illustration from scratch; do not edit, trace, crop, recolor, or restyle the photographed product.

Primary request: Create a magnified, mechanically coherent close-up of one generic traditional pipe-wrench head and its adjustment mechanism. The image should teach the relationship of the hook jaw, threaded shank, adjustment nut, and fixed heel jaw entirely through clear geometry, without labels or arrows.

Scene/backdrop: pure white square canvas with no scene, floor plane, border, callout, or decoration.
Subject and mechanism: Show one assembled pipe-wrench head. On the left, one curved movable full-floating hook jaw continues into one straight threaded shank as one continuous physical component. The same single shank stays on one clear axis, enters the body neck, and passes through exactly one clearly bounded knurled circular adjustment nut. Show a short aligned section of threaded shank immediately on both sides of that one nut; a short rounded shank end beyond the nut is acceptable. The opaque body may naturally hide a small middle part of the hook-jaw-to-shank connection, but all visible portions must align and no contradictory second component may appear. Below the hook jaw, one fixed heel jaw is integral to the body. Its serrated gripping face directly opposes the hook jaw's serrated inner face across one open pipe-gripping throat.

Style/medium: new original monochrome educational technical line art; crisp graphite-black outer contours, consistent medium interior lines, controlled pale-gray form washes, and sparse functional hatching. Invent neutral generic body, jaw, nut, and shank contours. Do not reproduce any source-specific outline, plate, fastener, texture, or knurl pattern.
Composition/framing: exact orthographic side close-up, no perspective and no visible top or underside planes. Head at left, threaded shank and nut extending right on a level axis. Fill roughly 82 percent of the square with the mechanism. Keep the complete hook jaw, fixed heel jaw, open throat, entire visible shank, entire single nut, and a short section of body/handle inside the frame with even white clearance. Intentionally omit most of the long handle so the adjustment mechanism is large and readable at 320 by 320 pixels.

Constraints: one assembled mechanism only; one hook jaw; one threaded shank; one adjustment nut; one fixed heel jaw; physically connected parts; opposed serrations; generic and unbranded; no text, pseudo-text, numerals, labels, arrows, circles, dimensions, answer cues, logos, watermarks, hands, pipe, extra tools, or additional parts.
Avoid: an exploded view; transparent housing; fictional cutaway; diagonal, rotated, three-quarter, top-down, or photographic view; adjustable-wrench crescent geometry, smooth parallel jaws, or worm gear; duplicated, forked, parallel, detached, floating, or misaligned shanks; a second nut, collar, rack, rod, gear, jaw, or loose fragment; fused jaws; same-facing teeth; impossible intersections; red, orange, or any color; glossy surfaces; shadows; reflections; copied branding, contours, proportions, holes, recesses, plates, fasteners, textures, trade dress, or source composition.
candidates.fatalFinding: The visible smooth hook-jaw stem entered the upper housing while the threaded segment exited lower on a different centerline, so the one-piece mechanism was not demonstrated. Two narrow side bands around the knurled center also weakened the exactly-one-nut reading at 320 pixels.
candidates.nonfatalPositives: The image had a strong orthographic close-up, complete meaning-bearing crop, opposed serrated jaws, clean monochrome treatment, and no text, branding, or source trade dress.
